discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics (2D materials, strongly correlated electrons)
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted, with a simple and elegant continuum model, that two graphene sheets twisted by a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees develop nearly flat electronic bands, where interactions dominate kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero and co-workers realised this regime experimentally, discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene. This marriage of predictive theory and exquisite device engineering created 'twistronics': a tunable platform in which the twist angle and a gate voltage control strong correlations, superconductivity, orbital magnetism, and quantum anomalous and fractional Chern insulating states. Moiré materials now serve as quantum simulators for problems once accessible only in complex oxides, and they have reshaped condensed matter physics worldwide. The discovery opened an entire new field and continues to yield fundamental surprises.
